title: Why India’s answer to China’s mega dam is facing resistance in Siang valley
content: In Arunachal Pradesh, the ambitious 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project has ignited fierce resistance from local tribes. They express fears about the potential displacement of over 150,000 residents and the loss of villages and farmland. While state officials assert that the pre-feasibility report is merely an early assessment, indigenous communities voice discontent over unauthorized survey actions and urge a reevaluation of the initiative.

title: Toxic foam returns to Yamuna as AQI touches 168, GRAP-1 restrictions in force
content: The air quality in Delhi-NCR has substantially deteriorated, with the Air Quality Index registering an alarming 168, indicating unhealthy conditions. Toxic foam has resurfaced on the Yamuna River, particularly around Kalindi Kunj. In response, the Commission for Air Quality Management has initiated Stage 1 of the Graded Response Action Plan.

title: Tensions flare in Hyderabad after eggs 'thrown' at idol during procession
content: Hindu organisations protested following an incident where eggs were allegedly thrown at a Durga Mata idol. The incident occurred during an immersion procession within Madanapet police station limits in Hyderabad. Police responded promptly after receiving a call and took the suspects into custody for investigation. A similar incident involving stone-pelting was reported during a Durga Visarjan procession in Maharashtra.

title: ‘VIP culture’ in hospitals can compromise patient safety, equitable care: AIIMS doctors
content: Pressure from influential patients can lead to unnecessary medical procedures and a longer recovery time for others. Surgical oncologists at AIIMS Delhi emphasize that this practice undermines equal treatment for all patients. Prolonged hospital stays for VIPs can also negatively impact hospital resources and staff morale. The authors advocate for appropriate clinical protocols and transparent admission criteria to ensure fair patient care.

title: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan shift donations towards AI and science
content: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan are investing $50 million to establish STEM labs and an AI center at Sacramento State University. This generous donation aims to transform vacant state office buildings into a thriving downtown campus. California Governor Gavin Newsom emphasized this initiative will enhance the tech job talent pipeline, while the couple shifts their philanthropic efforts toward biomedical AI, aligning with Meta’s vision for innovation and education.

title: India, Australia troops train for coastal, island warfare in AUSTRAHIND 2026
content: Indian and Australian army troops are actively participating in joint combat drills at the Foreign Training Node in Thiruvananthapuram, designated Exercise AUSTRAHIND 2026. This exercise, featuring approximately 240 servicemen including 120 from each country and a New Zealand observer team, is crafted to boost operational synergy with specialized activities such as combat swimming, ambush strategies, and focused aerial operations aimed at refining skills for joint coastal and island maneuvers.

title: New York court orders review of jailed mother's $500 child support cap claim
content: A New York woman serving a seven-year prison sentence for kidnapping her child has won a fresh hearing over unpaid child support. Chelsea Four-Rosenbaum had sought to limit her debt to $500, arguing that her income remained below federal poverty guidelines while imprisoned. An appeals court ruled that her request had been examined under the wrong legal provision and ordered a fresh review.

title: Protests engulf Europe: People take to streets in France, Albania, Italy, Spain, Portugal
content: Thousands of people protested across Europe over the weekend, demanding action against rising living costs and government corruption. Demonstrations were reported in France, Italy, Albania, Spain, and Portugal, with varying degrees of violence. Clashes between protesters and police resulted in numerous arrests and injuries in several countries. Many demonstrators called for affordable housing, better education, and protection of public pensions.

title: Kentucky court orders fresh review of $703,000 farm dispute after divorce
content: Mary and Fred Holden's property settlement agreed to equal ownership of their Kentucky farm. Disagreements arose regarding when the farm should be listed for sale after two years. After their son moved out, Mary requested the farm be sold or purchased by Fred. The appeals court found the agreement's wording ambiguous, requiring a fresh evaluation in family court.

title: Ashton Kutcher and Mila Kunis expand $10M beach house after mudslides
content: Ashton Kutcher and Mila Kunis are planning a significant renovation of their Carpinteria beachfront property. The proposed changes include expanding the main residence and adding a swimming pool. They acquired the property in 2017 for $10.1 million and have seen its estimated value rise to about $17 million. The couple's plans involve the removal of a guest cottage to enhance the outdoor living space.

title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang says US rules pushed China toward self-reliance
content: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang pointed out that US export controls have significantly fueled China's semiconductor advancements. He remarked that these restrictions have compelled China to bolster its own chip production strengths. Huang also expressed strong faith in the US technology sector's resilience, despite heightened competition from China, and dismissed worries about an impending memory chip surplus, predicting ongoing demand for High Bandwidth Memory in the years ahead.

title: IIT Madras graduates' hostel idea grows into over 1,500 foldable buildings
content: Modulus Housing, founded by IIT Madras graduates, focuses on manufacturing foldable buildings for quick assembly and transportation. Since 2018, it has provided over 1,500 modular structures across India and parts of Africa. The startup aims to improve access to essential infrastructure like schools and clinics, especially in rural areas. Recently, it raised ₹70 crore in funding to support further expansion and innovation.

title: Ukraine drone attacks kill three, injure 14 in Russia’s Belgorod region
content: A drone strike carried out by Ukrainian forces hit Belgorod, leading to two confirmed deaths and injuring at least 13 people. Local officials highlighted significant destruction to housing, vehicles, and local infrastructure. Additionally, a nearby village reported another fatality and injuries stemming from the ongoing hostilities. These events underscore the ongoing violence escalating along the Russia-Ukraine border, and tensions continue to mount in the region.

title: Market recap: Eight of top 10 firms lose Rs 1.55 lakh crore
content: HDFC Bank and Bajaj Finance experienced significant market value declines last week amid broader market losses. The combined drop in valuations for eight major companies totaled Rs 1.55 lakh crore. Market capitalization for BSE-listed companies fell sharply by Rs 20,78,774.28 crore. Only Tata Consultancy Services and Larsen & Toubro managed to increase their market valuations during this period.

title: In first-ever climate crisis amends, Nepal to get $21.6 million
content: The decision taken this week by the UN body, the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD), in its emergency meeting assumes significance as it is not only a kind of admission that climate change causes such extreme events, but also an endorsement of the principle that historical polluters (developed nations) must contribute to the fund to assist vulnerable developing countries.

title: ‘200 seats haq hai hamara’: Congress puts its UP poll ambitions on Lucknow walls
content: Posters demanding 200 Assembly seats have surfaced outside the Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee headquarters in Lucknow. Congress aims to strengthen its position ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections by negotiating a larger seat share. The party has reportedly submitted a wishlist to its ally, Samajwadi Party, complicating seat-sharing discussions. State Congress leaders are using a grading model to evaluate constituencies based on organisational growth.

title: Were they beheaded? Bangladesh seeks answers from Saudi over execution of 'couple'
content: Bangladesh has requested detailed information from Saudi Arabia about the execution of two citizens. The two individuals were executed for committing an indecent act inside a mosque in Makkah. A diplomatic letter was sent seeking clarification on their legal representation during trials and other circumstances. Dhaka is also looking for explanations regarding discrepancies in the charges against these citizens.

title: 'War or no war, our policies remain unchanged': Iran FM Araghchi amid fresh US strike fears
content: Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Tehran's policies will not change regardless of potential war. He warned that resuming conflict would alter the security landscape in the Strait of Hormuz significantly. Following recent comments from US President Donald Trump, fears of renewed military action against Iran are escalating. Araghchi emphasized the need for rationality to avoid another military confrontation.

title: Foreign investors withdraw Rs 48,056 crore in October as market selling continues
content: Foreign Portfolio Investors have withdrawn Rs 48,056 crore from Indian equities during October due to high crude oil prices. Selling eased slightly in a recent week, with some FPIs becoming net buyers for two days. Elevated oil prices and inflation concerns are contributing to deteriorating corporate earnings outlooks affecting investor confidence. Domestic institutional investors have somewhat mitigated the selling pressure on markets in recent weeks.

title: 'When will you score runs?' Babar Azam's weaknesses exposed by ex-Pakistan player
content: Babar Azam's recent performances in the ODI tri-series have raised concerns regarding his ability to convert starts into significant scores. He scored 45 against Sri Lanka and 34 against England, failing to build on important beginnings. Former cricketer Tanveer Ahmed has highlighted weaknesses in Babar's batting against spinners, incoming fast deliveries, and short balls. He emphasized the need for Babar to address these vulnerabilities to improve his performance.

title: ‘Give priority to local artisans’: PM Modi’s festive shopping appeal as Diwali approaches
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged citizens to support local artisans by prioritizing their products while shopping for festivals. He emphasized that doing so would strengthen the 'Vocal for Local' campaign and promote a self-reliant India. Modi highlighted successful local exports such as makhana and arhar dal to various international markets. Additionally, he discussed efforts aimed at reviving traditional skills and farming practices, including natural cotton cultivation.

title: From unfinished books to 10-second reels: Is reading becoming lost art?
content: The growing preference for short-form digital content is raising concerns about children’s ability to engage with books and sustain attention. Educationists and experts examine declining reading habits, the role of examination-driven learning, and the impact of digital distractions. Drawing on research and Kerala’s library movement, the story explores ways to rebuild deep reading through schools, families and communities.

title: Drone attack: Iran targets Kurdish opposition bases in Iraq
content: Iran's armed forces conducted a drone attack on the Komala group in Iraq's Kurdistan region. This operation reportedly caused significant damage and casualties to the group's infrastructure. Previous strikes on the Komala group have occurred since the regional conflict began in February. Iran accuses these opposition groups of receiving support from Israel, its longstanding adversary. The Kurdish opposition has denied allegations of receiving arms from Israel despite Iran's claims.

title: Five IPOs to hit Dalal Street next week, targeting nearly Rs 2,600 cr from investors
content: Between October 26 and October 29, five companies will debut their initial public offerings, aiming to raise an impressive Rs 2,600 crore from the primary market. These firms—EAAA India Alternatives, SFC Environmental Technologies, M K Sons Fine Jewels, BLS Polymers, and Bombay Coated and Special Steels—will utilize the capital for business expansion, working capital augmentation, and settling debts. More companies are gearing up for IPO launches set for November 5.

title: Centre rushes 250 RAF personnel to Arunachal after protests over hydropower project
content: The Centre has deployed two Rapid Action Force companies comprising around 250 CRPF personnel to Arunachal Pradesh following violent protests against the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project. A mob torched an NHPC office and a police station in Pasighat, injuring over 40 police personnel. The project, seen as a strategic counter to China’s mega dam, faces opposition from indigenous tribes fearing displacement and submergence of villages.

title: Man spits gutkha from 3rd-floor balcony, dies after coming in contact with 11kV wire
content: Prabhulal Gupta, a 65-year-old man, tragically died in Ganjbasoda after an apparent accident involving an overhead power line. Residents reported that his spit, while chewing gutkha, made contact with the 11kV line. Locals expressed anger towards the electricity company for neglecting their complaints about unsafe wiring. His landlord mentioned that officials had assured residents about addressing these high-tension line concerns.

title: ‘Failed to pay rent’: How landlord’s complaint led to 1,600 fake Rs 500 notes
content: After a complaint from a concerned landlord, the Wathoda police raided a rented apartment, revealing a trove of counterfeit Rs 500 notes, printing machinery, and a laptop. Preliminary findings suggest that this operation may be connected to an extensive counterfeit currency syndicate. The principal suspect, Pushpam Bhandane, remains at large, prompting a coordinated search effort involving the anti-terrorism squad and other investigative bodies.

title: 'Don't be spectator, show leadership': EAM Jaishankar to UN on terrorism, global crises
content: In his latest statements, external affairs minister S Jaishankar called for a more robust leadership from the UN to confront pressing world issues. He highlighted a significant gap in global decision-making that leaves many regions, particularly in the Global South, behind in critical areas like finance, fuel, food, and fertilizer. Emphasizing the importance of fair AI development, Jaishankar encourages strategies that ensure widespread access to its benefits, fostering international cooperation.

title: From 14 medals to 114: How India achieved more with fewer athletes at Asian Para Games
content: India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi-Nagoya. That was considerably fewer than the 309 athletes listed for the Hangzhou campaign in 2023, yet the team surpassed its previous best by six medals.

title: Trump claims US has secured Greenland, Venezuela in ‘greatest real estate deal’
content: Donald Trump asserted at a rally that the United States has secured Greenland and Venezuela as territories. His statements were made despite the lack of legal transfer of sovereignty over Greenland from Denmark. A recent memorandum of understanding focused on maritime cooperation, which does not include Greenland. Trump also announced a significant investment by Audi in Georgia, emphasizing job creation.

title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million mansion faces fresh setback as neighbors object
content: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion faces fresh delays as neighbors challenge his landscaping and fencing plans. Residents have raised concerns about wildlife safety, lake views and potential damage to an aging sewer line, with one neighbor citing $75,000 in repair costs. Kelce’s construction team says it has spent $7,500 on sewer repairs and adjusted the plans. However, local officials require further changes before the remaining landscaping work can proceed.

title: ‘Buy me Thar’: Woman slapped, kicked, dragged by hair by husband over vehicle demand
content: A 28-year-old woman has taken the brave step of reporting her husband after an alleged assault sparked by a dispute over a vehicle. CCTV footage depicts the disturbing encounter, while neighbors came to her aid upon hearing her screams. Police are currently eyeing the medico-legal report as they prepare to move forward with the case.

title: Stock market outlook: Fed meeting, crude & more - top cues guiding Dalal Street this week
content: As Dalal Street braces for a pivotal week, key earnings reports and the impending US Federal Reserve interest rate decision are grabbing attention. Investors are eagerly anticipating the September industrial production and manufacturing figures, set to be released on October 28. Moreover, Jio Platforms' stock market entry promises to sway investor sentiment.

title: Watch: Protesters launch fireworks at police as fiery clashes take place in Albania
content: Protests in Tirana escalated into clashes as demonstrators faced off with riot police during an anti-government rally. Protesters expressed their anger over alleged government corruption, unemployment, and education issues. The demonstrations also targeted government buildings and banks, leading to significant unrest in the city. The student-led protests represented a wider movement against corruption and called for governmental reforms.

title: Devdutt Padikkal, Sai Sudharsan hit back after KL Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal failures
content: India A struggled initially but found stability through an unbeaten partnership between Devdutt Padikkal and Sai Sudharsan. Padikkal scored 56 runs, while Sudharsan contributed 39 runs, helping the team recover. After a poor start, the duo added 96 runs without losing another wicket by the end of Day 2. Earlier, India's bowlers did well as Anshul Kamboj and Auqib Nabi took three wickets each.

title: 'Thanks BJP for promoting': Rahul takes swipe at govt over Nov 1 rally in Delhi
content: On November 1, Rahul Gandhi is set to lead a rally to rally citizens against alleged vote theft, spotlighting issues like voter list inaccuracies and the response to complainants. The BJP has voiced concerns over the timing due to its proximity to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots memorial. Several organizations, including Delhi's Chamber of Trade and Industry, have expressed disapproval.

title: Judge who awarded 36 death sentences in 16 months transferred to family court
content: Judge Ravi Kumar Diwakar has been transferred to the family court after awarding multiple death sentences. He gained national attention for his decisions in Muzaffarnagar, including a notable case of a husband burning his wife. His tenure included recalling numerous pending cases, raising questions regarding administrative authority. Diwakar previously faced threats following his involvement in a high-profile mosque survey case.

title: Toddler killed by 24-yr-old elder brother inside Bihar temple
content: A one-and-a-half-year-old boy was allegedly murdered inside a Durga temple in Patna district. The accused, Ajit Kumar, is the elder brother of the victim, Manish Kumar. Police believe that Ajit used a sharp agricultural tool in the commission of the crime. Investigators are examining the motive and circumstances surrounding the tragic incident. Evidence is being collected to establish a clearer picture of the events that occurred.

title: 'He was a fish out of water': Sooryavanshi's No. 3 role questioned after 2nd T20I
content: Ravichandran Ashwin feels Vaibhav Sooryavanshi struggled at No. 3 in India’s second T20I against New Zealand, scoring just four runs off eight balls. He believes Sanju Samson should bat at No. 3 if Sooryavanshi, Abhishek Sharma and Samson play together. Ashwin also praised India’s middle order, highlighting the power and temperament of Tilak Varma, Nitish Kumar Reddy and Ramandeep Singh.

title: Mystery surrounds death of Class 12 student found burnt behind Delhi school guard room
content: An 18-year-old girl was discovered burnt behind the guard room of a school in Krishna Nagar. Police received a call regarding the fire incident and promptly arrived at the scene. They conducted preliminary proceedings and collected materials from the spot, including the victim's school bag. A crime team thoroughly inspected the location to gather evidence for the ongoing investigation.

title: Clashes break out at Jamia protest, campus shut, classes go online
content: Jamia Millia Islamia has opted for an online class format and closed its physical campus amid escalating student protests. Demonstrators are campaigning for the reinstatement of their student union, which has been non-existent since 2006. Tensions soared when security forces reportedly used aggression against hunger strikers. The administration has asked students to halt protests, following unsuccessful dialogue attempts, with the campus remaining shut for safety.

content: Nearly 30 leaders of various organisations discussed revising the minimum selling price for sugar and a higher Fair and Remunerative Price for sugarcane

content: NMDC, which caters to India's one-fourth iron ore demand, has set a goal to earn at least 20% of revenues from sale of minerals other than the key steel making raw material

content: He refused to disclose which party he would be joining after being expelled from JD(U), Mr. Singh rather went one step ahead claiming that he would float his own political party.

title: Nilgiris district hit by 62 minor landslips in a day till October 25 morning
content: The Nilgiris district recorded a cumulative total rainfall of 453.9 mm during the 24-hour period. Parsons Valley in Udhagamandalam taluk recorded the highest rainfall in the district at 52 mm.

title: A development dream linked to Ravana’s birthplace
content: In Greater Noida’s Bisrakh, where Dasara passes without the burning of Ravana’s effigy, the priests of two temples that are barely 300 metres apart claim that their temple stands at the exact spot where the Ramayana’s demon-king was born. Ishita Mishra finds that as the priests vie for Ravana’s legacy, residents hope that a story passed down through generations will bring their village recognition, roads, footfall, and funds

content: The police urge everyone to strictly adhere to the MCC and refrain from activities that can disturb public peace and order

content: Officials said investigators would verify whether Diya Krishna had merely liked the controversial post or crossed a legal line by commenting, sharing, advocating, or promoting the post that risked creating communal tensions in Keralam

content: Guidelines favour patient education, physical activity and exercise, with imaging reserved for cases where serious disease is suspected, say doctors

content: The ISRO chief said that the upcoming Kulasekarapattinam spaceport facility will feature crucial infrastructure such as integration buildings, launch pads, rail-track systems, telemetry, tracking, and command systems

content: In India’s largest district, industrialisation, mining, and shrinking grazing grounds are driving a steep decline in its camel population; once home to thousands of these beasts, Gujarat’s Kutch now faces the prospect of their disappearing from the landscape altogether
